title: Bhakti Saints Shankaracharya
definition: Adi Shankaracharya (788–820 CE) was a 8th-century Indian philosopher and theologian who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta, revitalizing Vedic tradition against the rising influence of Buddhism and Jainism.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the intellectual transition from post-Gupta Buddhism to the revival of Brahmanical Hinduism, forming the bedrock of the Bhakti movement.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Saints Shankaracharya.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Upanishads and Brahma Sutras
